name: table
summary: A data grid: a caption, column headers and rows of cells, scrolling sideways inside its own region when it is wider than the screen; rows can be one link each, and columns can sort on a header press.

properties.name: caption
properties.description: What the table is. It names the table, and the caption is shown above it unless hideCaption is set.

properties.name: hideCaption
properties.description: Hides the caption visually and keeps it as the table's name.

properties.name: columns
properties.description: The column headers, in order, separated by commas. The first column is the rows' header, what each row is.

properties.name: sortable
properties.description: The headers of the columns a press sorts, separated by commas. Each is a button; a press sorts ascending and the next press reverses.

properties.name: sortedBy
properties.description: The header of the sorted column, if any.

properties.name: sortDirection
properties.description: Which way the sorted column is sorted.

properties.name: sortedLabel
properties.description: What a screen reader hears after a sort, "Sorted by {header}, {direction}" by default.

properties.name: rowHref
properties.description: Makes each row one link, named by its row header, with one tab stop; buttons and links inside a cell keep their own presses. Web takes the address as a string or function; native kits take the press.

properties.name: dense
properties.description: Tighter cells, for many rows. A linked row is still 44 points tall on a touch screen.

properties.name: stickyHeader
properties.description: Keeps the header row at the top while the rows scroll under it.

properties.name: empty
properties.description: What the body shows when there are no rows, in one cell across every column. Default "Nothing here yet.".

slots.name: rows
slots.description: The body: rows separated by semicolons, cells in a row separated by bars. The first cell of a row is its row header.

events.name: sort
events.description: A sortable header was pressed: the column and its new direction.

events.name: press
events.description: With rowHref, a row was pressed: its index.

states.name: rest
states.description: Headers and rows, with the sorted header in the foreground colour and an arrow for its direction.

states.name: hover
states.description: A pointer over a sortable header or a linked row shades it.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A header or linked row being pressed is drawn so on its first frame; nothing scales.

states.name: focused
states.description: A sortable header or linked row with keyboard focus: the platform's focus ring.

states.name: busy
states.description: Not used: a table shows the rows it is given.

accessibility.name: The table is named by its caption; each column by its header; a sorted column reads as sorted, ascending or descending. The agent tree flattens a row into one node named by its cells in order, joined by commas, and a header is a heading (a button when it sorts) there: the native kits keep the real header, row and cell roles. A linked row is named by its row header and opens its destination.
accessibility.keyboard: A sortable header and a linked row are each one tab stop; Enter or Space presses a header, Enter follows a row's link. Buttons and links inside cells keep their own tab stops.
accessibility.web: A table with a caption, th scope=col column headers, a th scope=row row header per row, aria-sort on the sorted header, the sort announced in a polite live region, and a scroll region named by the caption.
accessibility.apple: A table of rows with accessibility headers; the sorted column announces its direction.
accessibility.windows: A UI Automation Table: ControlType.Table with the Grid and Table patterns (RowOrColumnMajor, ColumnHeaders), a ControlType.Header row holding one ControlType.HeaderItem per column (a sortable one also takes the Invoke pattern), a ControlType.DataItem per row, and ControlType.Text cells. The sorted direction is in the header's name (", sorted ascending") and the sort is announced through UI Automation notifications.
accessibility.android: A column with CollectionInfo of the row and column counts; each cell, header cells included, carries a CollectionItemInfo with its row and column index (header cells with isHeading), and a row groups its cells with mergeDescendants so TalkBack reads it in one stop, or for a linked row presses as a button named by its row header. A sorted header has a stateDescription, and a sort is announced with a live region.

deviations: Web takes columns as { key, header, cell, align, sortable, sortValue } and rows as objects, sorts them itself or reports onSortChange, and takes rowHref as an address; native kits take string cells and report press and sort.
Web's alignment, wrap, rowKey and external-link options (rowExternal, externalLabel) are not part of the native spec.
